title: Jonah and the Orchard
premise: Ada Thornbury built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly answering, for ten years, the letters of an anonymous pen pal who once kept her from disappearing. When her estranged grandmother's orchard—and the neighboring cottage—are left to her in a will contested by relatives who want it sold, Ada discovers her correspondent, Rowan Hale, has moved into that cottage to help fight the same legal battle. As they work together to prove the will's true intent outside a court system stacked against them, Ada must finally let herself be seen, choosing love and the orchard over the safe invisibility of her old life.
about_author: U. M. Vane is the pen name of a former estate paralegal who spent years watching families fracture over inheritances and decided fiction could deliver fairer verdicts. They write from a converted potting shed surrounded by apple trees they refuse to prune on schedule.

chapters.title: The Last Wedding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the lavish wedding she's producing, Ada watches a bride cry alone before the ceremony and feels nothing but recognition—she stopped believing in weddings after her own engagement collapsed. That night she rereads a decade-old letter from 'J,' the anonymous pen pal who once talked her off a ledge. Emotional beat: numbness cracked by longing.

chapters.title: Terms of the Will
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A solicitor's letter summons Ada: her estranged grandmother has died, leaving her Halfpenny Orchard with one condition—that she live there a full year or the land passes to developers backed by her uncle Gerald. Ada plans to sell fast and return to London. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knows
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rowan Hale arrives at the cottage next door, hired by a heritage trust to contest the development scheme. When Ada introduces herself, Rowan goes pale—they recognize her handwriting from ten years of letters. Rowan says nothing, terrified the truth will end the one honest relationship Ada has. Emotional beat: secret joy shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Forced together by the case, Ada and Rowan catalog the orchard's heirloom trees as evidence of its value beyond money. Their banter deepens into intimacy; Ada finds herself telling Rowan things she's never told anyone—including about J's letters. Rowan nearly confesses twice. Emotional beat: falling in love while lying by omission.

chapters.title: What Gerald Wants
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Uncle Gerald offers Ada a generous buyout, revealing he's been intercepting mail at the orchard for years—including letters addressed to her. Ada realizes some of J's letters never arrived, explaining silences she'd mourned. She refuses the buyout, choosing the fight. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Searching the cottage, Rowan finds drafts—dozens of unsent letters in their own hand, including one written the week Ada's engagement ended. The weight of the deception becomes unbearable just as Ada asks Rowan directly: 'Do you think J ever really existed?' Emotional beat: guilt reaching critical mass.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In probate court, Gerald's lawyers paint Ada as an absentee granddaughter; the case teeters until Rowan testifies about the orchard's living history. But afterward, celebrating, Ada finds one of Rowan's draft letters fallen from a coat pocket—in J's unmistakable phrasing. Emotional beat: triumph ambushed by betrayal.

chapters.title: Winter Without Words
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ada cuts Rowan off; the year-long residency condition looms, and without the trust partnership the legal case stalls. Rowan writes one final letter and leaves it unsigned in Ada's mailbox—the truth, plainly told, asking nothing. Ada reads it eleven times. Emotional beat: cold silence slowly thawing toward forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Verdict Outside the Court
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rather than appeal, Ada gathers the town—orchard workers, neighbors, the solicitor—to invoke an old common-law dedication her grandmother secretly recorded, protecting the land publicly and permanently. Gerald concedes. In the crowd, Ada finally speaks Rowan's name aloud, not as neighbor but as J. Emotional beat: justice won by community, not law.

chapters.title: First Fruit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. One year to the day, Ada's residency condition fulfilled, she plants a new tree with Rowan and hosts no wedding at all—just a promise exchanged under the blossoms, witnessed by the found family the fight created. She answers J's first letter at last, in person. Emotional beat: love chosen in the present tense.
